title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1RC---_1LD1RE_1LE0LD_1RA0LF_0RC0RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1RC---_1LD1RE_1LE0LD_1RA0LF_0RC0RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Sampled with the head in E at the left end, the tape is 1^X c 0000 (10)^s1 110 (10)^s2 110 …: a number X and a stack. Two rules of the map are clean (observed without exception after the first few samples); the folding of a non-empty stack is not decoded. Shift rules are proved in Lean.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Shift rules, for every length
claims.text: Going right: A turns 110 into 011, E turns 011 into 101 and 0001 into 1111, C turns 1010 into 0101 and 1000 into 1111; each for every n and every tape around.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 13,850 cells have been visited and 10,784 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.072). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496).

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c: 1010 steps from blank tape without a halt (29,751 ones).

claims.title: No closed tape language from windows up to 7
claims.text: bbtools.ctl with K = 2 to 7 closes but allows a halt (6 to 1,344 abstract halting configurations); n-gram CPS (widths 3 to 7, -H, -U) fails.

claims.title: The stack map
claims.text: At the 69 samples to 2.9·1010 steps (head in E on a 0 at the left end, c = 1110, a = 10, b = 110) the tape is 1^X c, then either nothing (empty stack) or 0000 a^s1 b a^s2 b …. Empty stack: X ≡ 0 (mod 4) gives X' = 3X/2 + 2, empty (1424 → 2138, 4240 → 6362); X ≡ 2 gives X' = X/2 + 3 with stack [(X−2)/4] (76,954 → 38,480, [19,238]); 20 of 20 cases from X = 18 on. Non-empty stack, X ≡ 0 (mod 4): X' = X/2, push X/4, top minus 1 (1072 [534] → 536 [268, 533] → 268 [134, 267, 533] → 134 [67, 133, 267, 533]); every case. Non-empty stack, X ≡ 2: the stack is folded back into a larger X (for one entry, X' = X + 3s + 5: 12,118 [6,057] → 30,294), not decoded in general.

claims.title: Where a halt would come from
claims.text: The halt is B reading a 1. B is entered from F reading a 1 (about 125 million times in 10<sup>9</sup> steps) or from A reading a 0; in all of them B read a 0.

claims.title: Does it halt?
claims.text: Not known. The fold of a non-empty stack, and which configurations of the map can put B on a 1, are open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 13,850 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A number and a stack
html: Each time the head is in E on a 0 at the left end, the tape (words a = 10, b = 110, c = 1110) is a run of X ones and a stack:
Between two samples the head sweeps across everything (the bouncer side); samples get rarer as the numbers grow (the logarithmic side).

sections.eyebrow: The rule from one sample to the next
sections.heading: Halve and push, or fold
html:
• X divisible by 4, stack non-empty: X is halved and X/4 is pushed; the old top loses 1 (the four lines above).
  • Empty stack, X ≡ 0 (mod 4): X becomes 3X/2 + 2 (1,424 → 2,138; 4,240 → 6,362).
  • Empty stack, X ≡ 2 (mod 4): X becomes X/2 + 3 and (X − 2)/4 is pushed (76,954 → 38,480 with stack [19,238]).
  • Non-empty stack, X ≡ 2 (mod 4): the stack is folded back into a bigger X; with one entry s, X' = X + 3s + 5 (12,118 [6,057] → 30,294). The general fold is not decoded.
Halving while divisible by 4 and growing by 3/2 otherwise is the shape of a Collatz-like map; the stack remembers the halvings, a little like the Hydra machines.

sections.heading: Only B on a 1
html: The only halt is B reading a 1. B comes right after F reads a 1 (or A reads a 0) and moves right, and in 1010 steps B always found a 0. Which configuration of the stack map could produce a 11 under F is not known; the question is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.072). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496).
After 109 steps the tape spans 13,850 cells (83 left of the start, 12,307 right), with a density of 1s of 0.779.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A stack machine on the tape: a leading run 1^X and a stack of blocks (10)^s; while 4 divides X the machine halves X and pushes X/4, and when X is 2 mod 4 the stack is folded back into a new X about 3/2 times larger (Hydra-like); the sweeps across the tape are the bouncer.
